A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same virtual-correspondence research, although v2 extends it to partially calibrated cameras. All pages, including equations, figures, tables, and supplementary material, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic experiments, noise tests, PhotoTourism evaluations on 10,000 image triplets, and supplementary two-view results on 9,900 image pairs.

after.justification: v2 reports original calibrated and partially calibrated pose evaluations, including PhotoTourism and KITTI results, controlled outlier tests, and parameter sensitivity experiments.

M1.justification: v2 replaces the Set Transformer with a shared-MLP/max-pooling network, changes its input from 5×6 to 4×6, revises normalization, and replaces the symmetric epipolar loss with a Sampson loss for a predicted shift. It also adds perturbation variants and 4p3vf solvers that generate two virtual correspondences and use 6pt+P3P for unknown shared focal length.

E1.justification: v2 adds the unknown-shared-focal-length task and KITTI driving imagery, plus controlled high-outlier scenarios on PhotoTourism. The original Cambridge Landmarks, ETH3D, and PhotoTourism coverage remains, including the supplementary two-view task.

E2.justification: v2 evaluates new consecutive 6pt, joint 6pt, 6pt+P3P, and 4p3vf(O) comparators for partially calibrated cameras (Table 2). In the retained two-view comparison, v1 Table 3's learned 4p(L) method is replaced by 4p(M±δ) in v2 Table 6. The original calibrated baseline families remain.

E3.justification: Reported training changes from 1,500 to 30 epochs and batches of 2,048 to 1,024. Synthetic scene size changes from 100×100×100 with camera distances 130–150 to 10×10×10 with distances 20–50; the 1M instances and 70/30 split remain. New protocols include controlled inlier ratios and iteration budgets, while KITTI uses AUC thresholds of 1°, 2.5°, 5°, and 10°.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled outlier robustness tests at inlier ratios 0.1, 0.2, and 0.4, and δ sensitivity sweeps (Figures 3 and 8–10; Tables 4–5). Noise tests extend to the new solver variants and partially calibrated task. Some separate second-pair error panels from v1 disappear, while combined pose and first-pair diagnostics remain.

E5.justification: Both versions use instance-level median and quartile boxplots with the same whisker convention, alongside average timings. Neither reports training seeds, uncertainty across repeated training runs, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Additional experimental instances and result rows do not establish a changed uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Many retained Table 1 entries change: Sacre Coeur AUC@5° for 4p3v(L) changes from 47.14 to 42.84, and for 4p3v(O) from 47.83 to 50.18. v2 adds KITTI, outlier, and δ-sweep results and replaces the two-view learned result. The changed learned model and timing hardware limit direct cross-version performance comparisons.

T1.justification: v2 Section 8 adds Lemma 1 and a geometric proof of the triangle-intersection property stated informally in v1 Section 3.3, supporting the existing virtual-correspondence distance bound. Section 3 also extends the degrees-of-freedom argument to unknown shared focal length. General pose-error propagation bounds remain unestablished.

C1.justification: The title, abstract, and contributions expand from calibrated 4p3v solutions to claimed first efficient solutions for the previously unsolved 4p3vf problem. v2 presents broader M- and L-based solver families and removes v1's concluding suggestion that 4p3v might have limited practical relevance. The general virtual-correspondence framework claim is retained.

C2.justification: v1 mainly anticipates an advantage under heavy outlier contamination; v2 interprets controlled iteration-based experiments as supporting that use case while retaining a preference for 5pt+P3P with fewer outliers and ample computation. New discussion addresses 6pt degeneracies, using a network trained for the calibrated problem, geometry-dependent δ selection, and the distinction between correspondence-error bounds and potentially large pose errors.

D1.justification: v2 documents the replacement network's layer widths, pooling, activations, and training recipe, plus δ choices and KITTI triplet construction. It newly specifies unbatched CPU inference and changes the reported CPU from i9-10900K to i9-10900X. Public release remains prospective; v2 promises solver source code, whereas v1 also explicitly promised the network and training data.

R1.justification: v2 positions the work as addressing a previously unsolved shared-focal-length problem, extending its novelty beyond competing calibrated solvers. It adds discussion of Ding et al.'s generalized three-view homotopy work and references supporting NeFSAC-style architecture, KITTI, and additional solver components. The established homotopy-continuation and epipole-search comparisons remain central.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, contribution list, discussion, and conclusion are substantially rewritten. Method exposition is reorganized into calibrated and partially calibrated cases, with mean-based methods presented before learned methods. General-framework discussion and detailed oracle/noise material move into a substantially reorganized, numbered supplement with a future-work section.

P2.justification: v2 adds outlier plots, a geometric proof illustration, a network architecture diagram, and KITTI and sensitivity tables. Calibrated solver timings move from a separate table into Table 1's final column. Noise figures are reorganized in the supplement with expanded legends and partially calibrated panels; the retained two-view table is renumbered and revised.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens validation: controlled outlier tests replace v1's speculation about practical usefulness with iteration-based evidence, while KITTI evaluations and δ sweeps test the framework's extension and design choices. The proof and implementation details strengthen its rationale and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the removed learned two-view comparison and lower reported AUC of the revised learned solver; hardware changes still limit cross-version timing conclusions.
